steps.sub: Give p and the effect size

eyebrow: A/A test: the null is true, 5,000 runs
code:
ps = np.empty(5000)
for i in range(5000):
    a = rng.normal(55, 15, 40)
    b = rng.normal(55, 15, 40)
    ps[i] = stats.ttest_ind(
        a, b, equal_var=False).pvalue
print((ps < 0.05).mean())  # 0.0488
print((ps < 0.50).mean())  # 0.5
caption: Under a true null, p-values are spread evenly.

eyebrow: Significant is not the same as important
code:
a = rng.normal(55.0, 15, 200000)
b = rng.normal(55.3, 15, 200000)
r = stats.ttest_ind(b, a,
                    equal_var=False)
print(round(b.mean() - a.mean(), 3))
print(r.pvalue)   # 1.8e-15
print(round((b.mean() - a.mean())
            / 15, 3))   # 0.025
caption: Tiny p, tiny effect: about 0.025 standard deviations.
